name: Odesli / Songlink API
type: Metadata-resolver / cross-platform link-resolution identifier (not audio fingerprinting)
maintainer: Odesli, Inc. (formerly branded 'Songlink'; widely reported in the ecosystem to have been acquired by Linktree circa 2022, but this could not be independently reconfirmed against a primary source in this research pass). [uncertain]
method: Given a URL from one streaming/media platform (or a {platform,type,id} triple such as an ISRC), Odesli looks up the matching entity across ~15+ other platforms (Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, YouTube Music, Deezer, Tidal, Amazon Music, SoundCloud, Pandora, Google Play, Napster, Bandcamp, Audius, Audiomack) via its own internal catalog-matching database and returns the equivalent links/IDs on each. It is pure metadata/ID cross-referencing, not audio analysis.
required_input: A URL (e.g., a youtube.com/watch?v= link) OR a platform+type+id triple (e.g., platform=isrc,type=song,id=<ISRC>); no audio or video file is required.
minimum_clip_length: 0s - no audio needed at all; resolution is triggered purely by URL/ID/text input.
classification_or_hitrate: Not a classifier. 'Hit rate' = whether the queried YouTube URL exists in Odesli's cross-platform catalog. No published numeric coverage/hit-rate statistic was found. Real-world production usage (e.g., a GitHub PR in the SpotiFLAC project titled 'Fix Songlink/Odesli API failures: direct Tidal search, retry, cache') shows developers have had to add retry/caching/fallback logic to handle Odesli failing to resolve some tracks, implying a non-trivial miss rate especially for less-mainstream content. [uncertain]
pitch_speed_cover_robustness: Not applicable in the audio-fingerprinting sense (no audio analysis). Robustness depends entirely on whether the specific YouTube video is the official/rights-holder-linked upload already present in Odesli's catalog; sped-up/nightcore/pitch-shifted fan reuploads or live-version videos not independently catalogued on other platforms will simply fail to resolve a match rather than being misidentified.
catalog_language_bias: No published breakdown. Coverage tracks the union of the ~15+ platforms it cross-references, so content with an official presence on Spotify/Apple Music/Deezer etc. (Western mainstream, K-pop, J-pop, C-pop with DSP distribution) resolves well, while independent/unclaimed/fan-made/VTuber content not distributed to major DSPs will have no cross-platform match at all, regardless of the YouTube upload's popularity. [uncertain]
evaluation_dataset: None published. This is a production consumer link-resolution product, not benchmarked against AudioSet, GTZAN, MUSAN, MagnaTagATune, or MAEB - it does not use audio-classification techniques at all.
confidence_calibration: No numeric confidence score is returned. Effectively binary per platform: either the platform's entry appears in entitiesByUniqueId/linksByPlatform (match found) or it is absent (no match). No tunable threshold exists because there is no continuous score to threshold.
api_availability: Unauthenticated /links calls are limited to 10 requests/minute. An optional API key historically raised this to roughly 60 requests/minute and was obtainable by emailing developers@song.link (still stated in some maintained third-party client libraries), but a separate current source states 'Odesli has stopped giving out API keys' and now directs production/sustained-access requests to an allowlisting form referenced in a 'Sunsetting the Songlink (Odesli) public API' help-center article that could not be directly fetched in this session (DNS/redirect issues). A third-party aggregator also reported a deprecation notice with an announced retirement date of July 31, 2026 for the whole v1-alpha.1 API namespace, after which it may return HTTP 410; this was not independently confirmed against Odesli's own primary documentation. No official public paid-tier pricing was found. [uncertain]
chrome_extension_usability: The /links endpoint is a simple unauthenticated GET with query parameters, which is architecturally well-suited to direct client-side fetch from a Chrome extension, but CORS headers on api.song.link were not independently verified via a direct request in this session (help.song.link, a different host, failed DNS resolution when tested). Should be confirmed with a live OPTIONS/GET+Origin header check before relying on it as CORS-open. [uncertain]
audio_access_requirement: None - no audio access is needed at all; only the YouTube URL or video ID string is required as input.
client_vs_server: Only the YouTube video URL/ID leaves the client toward Odesli's servers - no raw audio or user audio stream is involved either way. This is a comparatively strong privacy posture versus audio-fingerprinting approaches, though the fact of which video the user is viewing is still disclosed to a third-party server.
bundle_weight_cold_start: No model or library needs to be bundled; a single lightweight HTTPS GET request per lookup. Cold-start is dominated by Odesli's own backend latency cross-referencing multiple DSP catalogs, informally reported by users of client libraries as low-hundreds-of-ms to a couple of seconds depending on caching state; no formal SLA was found. [uncertain]
breakage_risk: High and apparently rising - multiple independent signals found in this session: (1) conflicting reports on whether new API keys are still issued at all, (2) a real production project (SpotiFLAC) needed to add retry/cache/fallback logic specifically to cope with Odesli API failures, (3) a reported hard deprecation/retirement timeline (July 31, 2026) for the entire public API namespace, and (4) the community-maintained songlink/docs GitHub repo is itself labeled '[Deprecated, possibly still accessed]'. This is the single highest long-term dependency risk among the items researched in this batch. [uncertain] on the exact retirement date's accuracy since it came from a third-party aggregator rather than Odesli's own primary docs.
realtime_capability: Individual lookups are architecturally lightweight (a single metadata GET), likely fast enough for near-instant in-browser use, but the unauthenticated 10 requests/minute cap makes it unsuitable for high-frequency or bursty in-browser usage across many users without a shared cache or a pooling backend proxy.
identification_fields: Response includes entitiesByUniqueId (keyed per platform entity, containing title, artistName, thumbnailUrl, apiProvider, platforms) and linksByPlatform (the resolved URL per platform such as spotify, appleMusic, youtube, youtubeMusic, deezer, tidal, amazonMusic, soundcloud), plus a unified pageUrl (song.link share link). No numeric match-confidence score is included. [uncertain] on whether artistName is a string or an array depending on the SDK/version consulted.
isrc_availability: Conflicting evidence found. The API definitely accepts an ISRC as an input identifier for querying (platform=isrc,type=song,id=<ISRC>), but sources disagree on whether ISRC is present as an output field within entitiesByUniqueId - one summarized description claimed an ISRC field is extractable from entities, while the official response-shape description found elsewhere did not list it. This was not independently confirmed via a live API call in this session. [uncertain]
karaoke_specific_outputs: None - no BPM, musical key, vocal/instrumental activity, or word-level lyric timing; the service only resolves title/artist/cross-platform links.
tos_restrictions: Primary Terms of Service documentation (Notion-hosted help center) could not be fetched directly in this session, so exact clause wording is unconfirmed. Known constraints: 10 req/min hard cap without a key, and reportedly halted self-serve API key issuance with sustained/commercial access now funneled through an allowlisting request process rather than automatic approval. [uncertain]
risk_tolerance_note: This is an official first-party API (not a scraping or reverse-engineered surface), so there is comparatively little ToS gray area, but it is functionally being wound down as a self-serve product for new users. The practical risk to manage is business continuity/availability (it may become unavailable or heavily throttled) rather than legal risk - a fallback path (e.g., directly querying iTunes/Deezer/MusicBrainz instead of relying solely on Odesli) is advisable.
cascade_position: Best used as an enrichment/cross-referencing step after a video is already suspected to be music (e.g., following a cheap title-heuristic or classifier gate) - it cannot itself act as the music/non-music gate since it takes no raw audio and is not a classifier. When it does return a match, it is a low-cost, high-precision way to obtain canonical title/artist plus equivalent links on other platforms for further enrichment.
failure_mode: Fails silently/gracefully - an unmatched URL returns an empty or partial linksByPlatform/entitiesByUniqueId rather than a confidently wrong answer, since it performs real cross-platform ID/link matching rather than generative guessing.
cost_model_at_scale: No official public pricing tier for higher-volume/paid access was found in this session. The free unauthenticated tier is capped at 10 req/min, and combined with reports that new API keys are no longer routinely issued, there is no clearly advertised self-serve path to scale usage - a real constraint if this project expects meaningful per-session query volume. [uncertain]
geo_region_availability: Supports a userCountry parameter (two-letter country code, defaults to 'US') that controls which regional catalog/links are considered when resolving matches on each downstream platform; results can therefore vary by region since each linked platform (Spotify, Apple Music, etc.) applies its own regional licensing. No evidence the Odesli service itself is blocked in specific countries was found. [uncertain] on completeness of this picture.
